All-American Boys Game|2012]]) * First-team [[Parade All-America Boys Basketball Team|''Parade'' All-American]] (2012) }} '''Shabazz Nagee Muhammad''' (born November 13, 1992) is an American professional [[basketball]] player for the [[Piratas de La Guaira]] of the [[Superliga Profesional de Baloncesto]] (SPB). He played one season of [[college basketball]] for the [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA Bruins]] before being selected with the 14th overall pick in the [[2013 NBA draft]]. Muhammad went to [[Bishop Gorman High School]], where he was named [[Mr. Basketball USA]] and [[Naismith Prep Player of the Year]] in his senior year. He was one of the top rated college basketball recruits in the class of 2012. In his only season with UCLA, he earned [[NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors and was named to the [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|all-conference]] first team in the [[Pac-12 Conference|Pac-12]]; he was also voted [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-12 co-Freshman of the Year]]. ==Early life== Muhammad was born in [[Long Beach, California]] to Ron Holmes and Faye Muhammad. Ron Holmes was a {{convert|6|ft|5|in|m|adj=on}} standout, four-year starting [[point guard]] for the [[USC Trojans men's basketball]] program in the 1980s. Muhammad's mother, Faye, was a point guard and [[Track and field|track]] star at [[Long Beach State]]. Shabazz Muhammad is the second of three children. His older sister [[Asia Muhammad|Asia]] is a professional tennis player, and his younger brother Rashad played basketball in high school.{{cite news|last=Bensinger|first=Ken|title=NCAA to NBA millions: UCLA star's father mapped out a dream|date=March 22, 2013|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/news/columnone/la-fi-shabazz-muhammad-inc-20130322-dto,0,3133186.htmlstory|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130503174034/http://www.latimes.com/news/columnone/la-fi-shabazz-muhammad-inc-20130322-dto,0,3133186.htmlstory|archive-date=May 3, 2013|url-status=live}}{{cite news| url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/la-xpm-2012-apr-12-la-sp-0413-ucla-shabazz-buzz-20120413-story.html | work=Los Angeles Times | first1=Ben | last1=Bolch | first2=Baxter | last2=Holmes | title=There's quite a buzz about Shabazz Muhammad | date=April 12, 2012}}{{cite news|title=Shabazz Muhammad's 'killer instinct' at play|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/la-xpm-2013-jan-02-la-sp-0103-ucla-shabazz-muhammad-20130103-story.html | work=Los Angeles Times | first=Baxter|last=Holmes|date=January 2, 2013|access-date=January 2, 2013}} When Muhammad was six years old, he was diagnosed with [[Tourette syndrome]].{{cite web|url=http://dailybruin.com/2013/03/01/not-looking-back-shabazz-muhammad-overcomes-disorder-in-becoming-one-of-nations-best-players/|title=Not Looking Back: Shabazz Muhammad overcomes disorder in becoming one of nation's best players|work=DailyBruin.com|date=March 1, 2013|access-date=March 1, 2013}} ==High school career== Muhammad attended high school in [[Las Vegas Valley]] in [[Nevada]] at [[Bishop Gorman High School]], a Catholic high school with a $12,000 annual tuition that possessed a competitive athletics program. He became one of the few freshman to make their varsity basketball team. In his junior year, Muhammad led Bishop Gorman averaging 25.1 points and 7.7 rebounds for the season.{{cite web|url=http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/player?id=72514&_slug_=shabazz-muhammad&action=login&appRedirect=http://insider.espn.go.com/ncb/recruiting/player?id=72514&_slug_=shabazz-muhammad |title=Shabazz Muhammad |work=ESPN.com |access-date=July 15, 2011}}{{dead link|date=July 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} Muhammad was also named the 2011 [[Gatorade Player of the Year awards|Gatorade Player of the Year]] for the state of [[Nevada]]. Muhammad was the 2011–12 high school diary keeper for [[SLAM Magazine]].{{cite magazine|url=http://www.slamonline.com/online/college-hs/high-school/2011/10/shabazz-muhammad-diary-no-1/|title=Shabazz Muhammad, Diary 1|access-date=March 29, 2012|date=October 12, 2011|magazine=[[SLAM Magazine|SLAMOnline.com]]}} Muhammad played in the [[2012 McDonald's All-American Boys Game|2012 McDonald's All-American game]], where he led the West team to a 106–102 victory over the East team, and was named the MVP of the game with 21 points and 6 rebounds. Muhammad also participated in and won the 2012 Powerade Jam Fest Dunk Contest.{{cite magazine|url=http://sportsillustrated.cnn.com/2012/highschool/03/29/boys.mcdonalds.game/|title=Muhammad leads West 2012|access-date=November 17, 2012|newspaper=[[USA Today]]}} ==College career== [[File:Shabazz Muhammad UCLA.JPG|thumb|165px|left|Muhammad with [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]] in 2012.]] Boasting scholarship offers from scores of basketball programs, Muhammad's final list of schools was [[Duke Blue Devils men's basketball|Duke]], [[Kentucky Wildcats men's basketball|Kentucky]], and [[UCLA Bruins men's basketball|UCLA]]. On April 11, 2012, Muhammad announced he would attend UCLA.{{cite news|title=Vegas basketball prep star Shabazz Muhammad picks UCLA over Kentucky, Duke|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/vegas-basketball-prep-star-shabazz-muhammad-picks-ucla-over-kentucky-duke/2012/04/11/gIQAdyDSBT_story.html|work=washingtonpost.com|access-date=April 12, 2012|date=April 11, 2012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20181215230034/https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/colleges/vegas-basketball-prep-star-shabazz-muhammad-picks-ucla-over-kentucky-duke/2012/04/11/gIQAdyDSBT_story.html|archive-date=December 15, 2018|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|title=Shabazz Muhammad to UCLA|url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/story/_/id/7803515/shabazz-muhammad-no-2-overall-recruit-commits-ucla-bruins|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=April 12, 2012|date=April 11, 2012}} Muhammad was declared ineligible to play hours prior to UCLA's [[2012–13 UCLA Bruins men's basketball team|2012–13]] season opener against [[2012–13 Indiana State Sycamores men's basketball team|Indiana State]] due to alleged violations involving the NCAA's amateurism rules surrounding unofficial university visits.{{cite news|title=Shabazz Muhammad ruled ineligible for UCLA Bruins|url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/ncb/story/_/id/8612665/shabazz-muhammad-ruled-ineligible-ucla-bruins|publisher=[[ESPN]]|access-date=November 13, 2012|date=November 13, 2012}} The NCAA ruled he had received benefits for travel expenses and lodging from family friend Benjamin Lincoln, who had befriended Muhammad's father when Muhammad was in seventh grade, during unofficial visits to Duke and [[North Carolina Tar Heels men's basketball|North Carolina]].{{cite news|title=Race and the NCAA|url=https://www.nytimes.com/2012/11/20/opinion/nocera-race-and-the-ncaa.html?ref=joenocera&_r=0) | work=The New York Times | first=Joe|last=Nocera|date=November 19, 2012|access-date=November 19, 2012}} After missing three games and an appeal by UCLA, he was reinstated, and his family was required to repay approximately $1,600.{{cite news|last=Yoon|first=Peter|title=Shabazz Muhammad eligible to play|date=November 16, 2012|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/ncb/story/_/id/8640531/shabazz-muhammad-ucla-bruins-reinstated-ncaa|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121117081247/http://espn.go.com/los-angeles/ncb/story/_/id/8640531/shabazz-muhammad-ucla-bruins-reinstated-ncaa|archive-date=November 17, 2012|url-status=live}} Days before his reinstatement, several media outlets reported the boyfriend of the NCAA's lead investigator boasted publicly that the NCAA would find him ineligible eight days after the investigation commenced.{{cite news| url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/la-xpm-2012-nov-14-la-sp-1115-ucla-shabazz-ncaa-20121115-story.html | work=Los Angeles Times | first=Baxter | last=Holmes | title=Overheard conversation suggests NCAA prejudged Shabazz Muhammad case | date=November 14, 2012 |access-date=November 14, 2012 }} The NCAA subsequently fired the investigator that web|url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/mens-college-basketball/story/_/id/8768719/college-sports-fires-lead-investigator-shabazz-muhammad-case-according-report|title=Report: NCAA fires UCLA investigator|work=ESPN.com|date=December 20, 2012|access-date=December 20, 2012}} Muhammad scored 15 points off the bench in his debut in a 78–70 loss to [[2012–13 Georgetown Hoyas men's basketball team|Georgetown]] in the semifinals of the [[Legends Classic (basketball tournament)|Legends Classic]].{{cite news|last=Spector|first=Jesse|title=UCLA vs. Georgetown: Shabazz Muhammad's debut ends in defeat|date=November 19, 2012|work=sportingnews.com|url=http://aol.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2012-11-19/ucla-bruins-vs-georgetown-hoyas-score-shabazz-muhammad-debut-jordan-adams-stats|access-date=November 20, 2012|archive-date=February 3, 2013|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130203134524/http://aol.sportingnews.com/ncaa-basketball/story/2012-11-19/ucla-bruins-vs-georgetown-hoyas-score-shabazz-muhammad-debut-jordan-adams-stats|url-status=dead}} Times|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/college/basketball/la-sp-1121-ucla-georgia-20121121,0,1189838.story|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20121121112159/http://www.latimes.com/sports/college/basketball/la-sp-1121-ucla-georgia-20121121,0,1189838.story|archive-date=November 2012|work=WashingtonPost.com|url=https://articles.washingtonpost.com/2012-12-29/sports/36072099_1_shabazz-muhammad-laurence-bowers-phil-pressey}}{{dead link|date=October 2024|bot=medic}}{{cbignore|bot=medic}} He scored a game-high 23 points in an 84–73 road win over No. 6 [[2012–13 Arizona Wildcats men's basketball team|Arizona]].{{cite news|title=UCLA rides huge start to surprise No. 6 Arizona|date=January 24, 2013|work=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press|url=https://www.espn.com/mens-college-basketball/recap?gameId=330240012|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130125075240/http://scores.espn.go.com/ncb/recap?gameId=330240012|archive-date=January 25, 2013|url-status=live}} Muhammad received national recognition, earning second-team [[2013 NCAA Men's Basketball All-Americans|All-American]] honors from ''[[Sporting News]]'' and a [[Freshman All-American]] selection by the [[United States Basketball Writers Association]] (USBWA).{{cite news|title=Shabazz Muhammad Earns All-District, All-America Acclaim|date=March 26, 2013|work=UCLABruins.com|url=http://www.uclabruins.com/ViewArticle.dbml?DB_OEM_ID=30500&ATCLID=207910577|access-date=October 9, 2014}} He was also named to the [[List of All-Pacific-12 Conference men's basketball teams|All-Pac-12]] first team, and was voted the [[Pac-12 Conference Men's Basketball Freshman of the Year|Pac-12 co-Freshman of the Year]] along with [[Jahii Carson]] of [[Arizona State Sun Devils men's basketball|Arizona State]].{{cite news|last=Yoon|first=Peter|title=Shabazz Muhammad, Larry Drew II named All-Pac-12|date=March 11, 2013|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/ucla/post/_/id/13549/shabazz-muhammad-larry-drew-ii-named-all-pac-12|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130314032008/http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/ucla/post/_/id/13549/shabazz-muhammad-larry-drew-ii-named-all-pac-12|archive-date=March 14, 2013|url-status=live}} Muhammad finished the season averaging 17.9 points, 5.2 rebounds, 0.8 assists, 0.7 steals, and 0.1 blocks per game. He shot 44.3% from the floor and made 71.1% of his free throws.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/player/_/id/2993875/shabazz-muhammad|title=Shabazz Muhammad ESPN bio|work=ESPN.com|access-date=May 17, 2013}} While his scoring ability was unquestionable, he was not the flashy offensive player that was expected upon his signing. Muhammad struggled in the postseason, shooting 39.7 percent (23-for-58) and averaging 15.3 points in four games. He was 0-for-10 on [[three-point field goal]]s. During the season, he focused on shooting and rarely passed the ball.{{cite news|last=Zgoda|first=Jerry|title=Muhammad's career night helps Wolves rally past Phoenix|date=February 26, 2014|newspaper=Star Tribune|url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/247190181.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140302161833/http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/247190181.html|archive-date=March 2, 2014|url-status=live}} He was also a weak defensive player, though he did show improvement. ==Professional career== ===Minnesota Timberwolves (2013–2018)=== ====2013–14 season==== On April 16, 2013, Muhammad [[NBA draft declaration|declared]] he would enter the [[2013 NBA draft]].{{cite news|title=Shabazz Muhammad to turn pro|date=April 16, 2013|work=ESPN.com|agency=Associated Press|url=https://www.espn.com/los-angeles/nba/story/_/id/9178426/2013-nba-draft-shabazz-muhammad-one-done-ucla-bruins|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130417165428/http://espn.go.com/los-angeles/nba/story/_/id/9178426/2013-nba-draft-shabazz-muhammad-one-done-ucla-bruins|archive-date=April 17, 2013|url-status=live}} While he began his college career projected as a top-three draft pick, his stock fell to being viewed as a back-end [[lottery pick]].{{cite news|last=Yoon|first=Peter|title=With draft stock dropping, Muhammad decision is a no-brainer|date=April 16, 2013|work=ESPN.com|url=https://www.espn.com/blog/los-angeles/ucla/post/_/id/13747/with-draft-stock-dropping-muhammad-decision-is-a-no-brainer|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130522170832/http://espn.go.com/blog/los-angeles/ucla/post/_/id/13747/with-draft-stock-dropping-muhammad-decision-is-a-no-brainer|archive-date=May 22, 2013|url-status=live}} Muhammad was drafted 14th overall by the [[Utah Jazz]]; afterwards, his draft rights were traded to the [[Minnesota Timberwolves]] along with the 21st pick, [[Gorgui Dieng]], in exchange for the ninth pick, [[Trey Burke]].{{cite news|url=https://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/utah-jazz-grab-national-player-of-the-year-in-michigan-guard-trey-burke/2013/06/27/bf158de4-df9f-11e2-8cf3-35c1113cfcc5_story.html|archive-url=https://archive.today/20130629090646/http://www.washingtonpost.com/sports/wizards/utah-jazz-grab-national-player-of-the-year-in-michigan-guard-trey-burke/2013/06/27/bf158de4-df9f-11e2-8cf3-35c1113cfcc5_story.html|archive-date=June 29, 2013|title=Utah Jazz grab national player of the year in Michigan guard Trey Burke|access-date=June 28, 2013|date=June 27, 2013|newspaper=[[Washington Post]]|url-status=dead}}{{cite web|url=http://www.mlive.com/wolverines/index.ssf/2013/06/on_the_move_trey_burke_ends_up.html|title=On the move: Trey Burke ends up with Utah Jazz after being traded by the Minnesota Timberwolves|access-date=June 28, 2013|date=June 27, 2013|work=MLive.com|author=Baumgardner, Nick}} While attending the NBA's rookie transition program in August before the season, Muhammad was sent home due to a rules violation.{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/2013/news/08/07/muhammad-sent-home-from-rtp.ap/|title=Muhammad sent home from rookie transition program|work=NBA.com|date=August 7, 2013|access-date=August 7, 2013}} On January 5, 2014, Muhammad was [[assignment (NBA D-League)|assigned]] to the [[Iowa Energy]] of the [[NBA Development League]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-assign-shabazz-muhammad-iowa-energy|title=Wolves Assign Shabazz Muhammad To Iowa Energy|work=NBA.com|date=January 5, 2014|access-date=January 5, 2014}} In four games with Iowa, he averaged 24.5 points, shot 57.1% from the field, and had 9.8 rebounds per game. He played in the [[D-League Showcase]], and was named to the All-Showcase Team. On January 13, he was recalled by the Timberwolves.{{cite web|title=Wolves Recall Shabazz Muhammad From Iowa Energy|date=January 13, 2014|work=NBA.com|url=http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-recall-shabazz-muhammad-iowa-energy|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140116071002/http://www.nba.com/timberwolves/news/wolves-recall-shabazz-muhammad-iowa-energy|archive-date=January 16, 2014|url-status=live}} On February 8, with three teammates out injured, Muhammad scored 12 points in a 117–110 loss to the [[Portland Trail Blazers]].{{cite news|last=Youngblood|first=Kent|title=Shorthanded Wolves fall short|date=February 9, 2014|newspaper=Star Tribune|url=http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/244576601.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228072234/http://www.startribune.com/sports/wolves/244576601.html|archive-date=February 28, 2014|url-status=live}} After playing sparingly for the Wolves most of the season, it was his first game playing over 10 minutes.{{cite news|last=Robson|first=Britt|title=Wolves will enter March with flickering hopes — or flickering out?|date=February 27, 2014|work=minnpost.com|url=http://www.minnpost.com/sports/2014/02/wolves-will-enter-march-flickering-hopes-or-flickering-out|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140228212223/http://www.minnpost.com/sports/2014/02/wolves-will-enter-march-flickering-hopes-or-flickering-out|archive-date=February 28, 2014|url-status=live}} On February 25, Muhammad played a season-high 24 minutes and scored a season-high 20 points in a 110–101 win over the [[Phoenix Suns]]; he scored 10 points while playing the entire fourth quarter, and also had five of his six rebounds during that time. On April 5, he sprained the [[medial collateral ligament]] (MCL) of his right knee against the [[Miami Heat]], which forced him to miss the remainder of the season. He averaged 3.9 points per game for the season.{{cite news|last=Feldman|first=Dave|title=Two disappointing Timberwolves to miss rest of disappointing season|date=April 7, 2014|work=probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com|url=http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/04/07/two-disappointing-timberwolves-to-miss-rest-of-disappointing-season/|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140409041446/http://probasketballtalk.nbcsports.com/2014/04/07/two-disappointing-timberwolves-to-miss-rest-of-disappointing-season/|archive-date=April February 21, 2015, he was ruled out for the rest of the season after requiring surgery for a torn ligament in his middle finger.{{cite web|url=https://sports.yahoo.com/news/sources--minnesota-s-shabazz-muhammad-will-miss-remainder-of-season-234349198-nba.html|title=Sources: Shabazz Muhammad to have surgery, miss rest of season|work=Yahoo.com|date=February 21, 2015|access-date=February 21, 2015}} ====2015–16 season==== Muhammad was able to stay healthy throughout 2015–16, playing in all 82 games. He saw his minutes dip slightly, as he managed 20.5 minutes per game compared to 22.8 mpg in 2014–15. As a result, Muhammad's scoring fell by three points per game and his three-point shooting fell almost all the way back to his rookie season level—he was taking threes at a higher rate in 2015–16 than in his first two seasons combined.{{cite web|last=Spurlock|first=Randy|url=http://dunkingwithwolves.com/2016/04/25/timberwolves-player-review-shabazz-muhammad/|title=Timberwolves Player Review: Shabazz Muhammad|work=DunkingWithWolves.com|date=April 25, 2016|access-date=December 30, 2016}} He finished with an average of 10.5 points per game and even set a career high during the season with 35 points on April 5 in a 124–117 overtime win over the [[Golden State Warriors]].{{cite web|url=http://www.nba.com/games/20160405/MINGSW/gameinfo.html|title=Timberwolves shock Warriors 124–117 in overtime|work=NBA.com|publisher=Turner Sports Interactive, Inc.|date=April 5, 2016|access-date=April 6, 2016}} While his offense remained steady, Muhammad's defense was considered statistically poor. Among 462 qualified players in 2015–16, Muhammad ranked 461st in ESPN's "Defensive Real Plus-Minus" statistic, ahead of only [[José Juan Barea|J.J. Barea]]. ====2016–17 season==== Muhammad continued to struggle on the defensive end in 2016–17, which made it difficult for him to earn the confidence of coach [[Tom Thibodeau]] over the first two months of the season.{{cite web|url=https://www.espn.com/nba/recap?gameId=400899939|title=Wiggins, Towns lead Wolves over Bucks, 116–99|work=ESPN.com|date=December 30, 2016|access-date=December 30, 2016}} He broke out on December 30, 2016, scoring 22 points in 18 minutes off the bench against the [[Milwaukee Bucks]]. He scored 10 first-quarter points against the Bucks and hit his first four three-pointers of the game to help lead the Timberwolves to a 116–99 win. ====2017–18 season==== On September 15, 2017, Muhammad's uncle, [[Stephone Paige]], played nine seasons in the [[National Football League]] (NFL) with 377 career [[Reception (American football)|receptions]]. His aunt, [[Robin Holmes-Sullivan]], was a four-year starter for [[Cal State Fullerton Titans|Cal State Fullerton]]'s basketball team.{{cite news|last=Foster|first=Chris|title=Shabazz Muhammad looks to add to family history|date=April 12, 2012|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|url=https://www.latimes.com/sports/la-xpm-2012-apr-12-la-sp-sn-shabazz-ucla-20120412-story.html|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130528061921/http://articles.latimes.com/2012/apr/12/sports/la-sp-sn-shabazz-ucla-20120412|archive-date=May 28, 2013|url-status=live}} On March 22, 2013, it was revealed in a report from the ''[[Los Angeles Times]]'' that Muhammad was actually born exactly one year earlier than his thought-to-be birthday of November 13, 1993.{{cite news |url=http://www.latimes.com/news/columnone/la-fi-shabazz-muhammad-inc-20130322-dto,0,3133186.htmlstory |title=NCAA to NBA millions: UCLA star's father mapped out a dream |newspaper=Los Angeles Times |date=March 22, 2013 |access-date=March 22, 2013 |first=Ken |last=Bensinger}} A copy of his birth certificate on file with the Los Angeles County Department of Public Health shows that he was born at [[Long Beach Memorial Medical Center]] exactly one year earlier, which made him 20 years old at the time. ''Los Angeles Times'' assumes that this was to make Muhammad look better "competing against younger, smaller athletes, particularly in the fast-growing years of early adolescence", and compared the case to that of baseball's [[Danny Almonte]].{{cite news|last1=Bensinger|first1=Ken|last2=Stevens|first2=Matt|url=http://www.latimes.com/sports/sportsnow/la-sp-sn-shabazz-muhammad-20130322,0,1805254.story|title=Shabazz Muhammad's new age (20, not 19) could hurt draft status|newspaper=Los Angeles Times|date=March 22, 2013|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20130325064813/http://www.latimes.com/sports/sportsnow/la-sp-sn-shabazz-muhammad-20130322,0,1805254.story|archive-date=March 25, 2013|url-status=live}} Although Muhammad's father said the younger age in UCLA's media guide was "a mistake", numerous sources online show that Muhammad had been passing himself off as younger for years.{{cite video|title=PointguardU.com Shabazz Muhammad Interview from Las Vegas|url=https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=p_0zE6sYmuw|time=0:41|publisher=pointguardu.com|publication-date=July 24, 2009|access-date=May
